combinations.title: Highest risk — zk-recovery likely unavailable
combinations.text: Your coins are in P2PK addresses with permanently exposed public keys and no BIP-39 seed. If BIP 361 activates, your only recovery hope is Phase C, which may not support early wallet formats. Move them to a modern wallet as soon as P2MR is available.

combinations.title: High risk — public key exposed on first spend
combinations.text: If you have ever spent from this address, your public key is visible on-chain. BIP 361's sunset would eventually freeze any coins still in legacy formats. Migrate to a P2MR-compatible wallet before Phase A.

combinations.title: High risk — key-path spend exposed
combinations.text: Taproot key-path spends reveal your internal public key. BIP 360 removes this path entirely in P2MR. Re-send your taproot UTXOs to P2MR addresses once wallets support them.

combinations.title: Medium risk — migrate before Phase A
combinations.text: SegWit v0 (P2WPKH) still uses ECDSA and will be sunset. You likely have a seed phrase, so zk-recovery may work in Phase C, but do not rely on it. Migrate proactively.

combinations.title: High risk — identify your wallet first
combinations.text: Pre-2013 wallets are almost certainly P2PK or early P2PKH. Both have exposed public keys. Treat this as highest risk until you confirm otherwise.

combinations.text: Standard P2PKH addresses are vulnerable once spent. You have time, but do not wait until Phase B. Move to a P2MR-compatible wallet well before the deadline.

combinations.text: You have a modern seed phrase and SegWit v0 outputs. The risk is manageable if you migrate before Phase A (~3 years post-activation). Use this time to verify your backup and wait for wallet support.

combinations.text: Addresses starting with '1' are P2PKH; 'bc1q' is SegWit; 'bc1p' is Taproot. If you don't know, check your wallet's receive history or use a block explorer.

combinations.title: How to identify your wallet
combinations.text: Open your wallet and check a receive address. '1...' = legacy P2PKH (medium risk). '3...' = P2SH (medium risk). 'bc1q...' = SegWit (low risk if unspent). 'bc1p...' = Taproot (high risk due to key-path). If your wallet was created before 2013 or you mined early coins, treat as highest risk.
